entry.title: Roc'n Rope - Konami's 1983 arcade climber for the Commodore 64 via BrokenBytes
entry.content:
Broken Bytes has began a project to bring over Konami’s 1983 arcade classic Roc’n Rope to the Commodore 64 without any AI! This faithful conversion tasks players with ascending treacherous, multi-tiered stages using nothing but a harpoon gun and sheer determination to reach a mythical phoenix. Navigating the vertical landscapes requires timing, as players must anchor ropes across treacherous gaps and climb to safety while dodging a barrage of falling rocks, aggressive dinosaurs, and hostile cavemen. To survive the onslaught, climbers can blind foes with a flashlight, snatch up power pills and feathers for a competitive edge, and chain together actions to keep their high-score bonus ticking across four distinct environments—ranging from jungle ledges, icy caves, spinning wheels to a towering waterfall.

The presentation stands out by utilizing full-screen overscan to deliver an impressive 320×248 pixel playfield that bleeds directly into the C64 borders, keeping the HUD cleanly tucked below the action. The technical wizardry extends to the physics engine, which employs sub-pixel positioning and frame timing tailored to PAL refresh rates to recreate the exact feel of the original cabinet. Dynamic rope mechanics ensure that climbing feels perfectly fluid as well, with the software seamlessly shifting anchored rope segments into bitmap data when the screen becomes crowded with prehistoric threats. Finally the four detailed worlds within the game make full use of the C64 palette.

Credits

  • Code: Antonio Savona
  • Graphics: Steve Day
  • Music & sound: Aldo Chiummo

entry.title: Van Helsing - Could this be another C64 hit from GriffonSoft and Psytronik Software?
entry.content:
Psytronik Software, the retro-publishing powerhouse behind recent hits like Sherwood and Musketeer, has officially launched Van Helsing on the Commodore 64. Developed by GriffonSoft as their most ambitious project to date, this atmospheric side-scroller transports players back to the grim autumn of 1893. The story kicks off during a celebratory gathering at the Harker residence, marking Jonathan's return from Transylvania, which is abruptly shattered by a bloodcurdling scream. A horrific, winged creature tears through the balcony to abduct Lucy Westenra into the night, leaving behind nothing but a gruesome trail of blood. Stepping into the boots of the legendary monster hunter Van Helsing, players must bravely pursue the fiend directly into Dracula’s dark domain, fighting off hordes of terrifying enemies across eight massive, intricately detailed scrolling levels.


The game boasts ultra-responsive controls and a flawlessly animated protagonist. Combat is highly dynamic, giving players an arsenal of collectable weaponry to fend off Dracula's forces, alongside native two-button joystick support that separates firing from jumping for tighter platforming. The title offers global accessibility with native PAL and NTSC compatibility, and looks to run flawlessly on the Commodore 64 as well as modern setups like the C64 Mini, Maxi, and Ultimate. For retro collectors looking to physicalise their collection, the deluxe digital download bundle packages the full game alongside its official soundtrack, stunning promotional artwork, and printable disk labels and sleeves.

entry.title: Cauldron - Halloween Edition - A brilliant game from the 1980's gets an improvement via AI/Devil-System
entry.content:
Devil-System has resurrected Palace Software’s 1985 classic with the release of Cauldron: Halloween Edition for the Amstrad CPC. Originally designed by Steve Brown and Richard Leinfellner as a genre-blending platformer and horizontally scrolling shoot 'em up, the game follows a witch's perilous quest to defeat the "Pumpking" and claim her title as the Witch Queen. While the original release garnered praise for its dual gameplay modes and visuals, it was notoriously infamous for its punishing, excessive difficulty. This new edition helps that issue by packing in three distinct difficulty levels, a dedicated training mode for relaxed exploration, a built-in map, and modern conveniences like a pause feature, a high-score table, and essential game-saving capabilities across four supported languages.

More detail in the trees

Furthermore this improved version also includes both a "Classic" and "Enhanced" mode on every single disk, allowing players to choose between the familiar nostalgic aesthetic or a refreshed presentation featuring updated details such as the trees in the image above. Beneath the hood, the controls and physics have been completely overhauled as well introducing gradual acceleration, gentle braking, and fluid animations to match. Combined with optimized rendering and a tuned gameplay pace, navigating the treacherous world on a broomstick has never felt smoother. Although purists like us, would probably prefer to stick to the insanely difficult original loaded up on a green screen monitor ;)

entry.title: Super Mario Land ZX - Gameboy Super Mario Land arrives on the ZX Spectrum via AI/kirby2000
entry.content:
Kirby2000 has released a public beta of Super Mario Land ZX for the ZX Spectrum 128K. This AI demake crams Nintendo's entire 1989 Game Boy launch title into a single 128K load. Players can tackle all 12 levels across four distinct worlds using either a keyboard or a Sinclair joystick. Every single element of the original looks to have been converted, including the memorable submarine and aeroplane shoot-’em-up stages, alongside 18 tunes rearranged for the Spectrum's AY audio chip. While the game is in beta however, the creator is currently seeking community feedback on this early build, expressing a particular interest in how the software performs when running on real, hardware.

The original game boy version sold 25 million copies, cementing itself as the fourth best-selling Game Boy title of all time. Though brief, the 1989 original was highly praised for successfully shrinking Mario's side-scrolling formula into a pocket-sized handheld experience, notably introducing Princess Daisy to the franchise (wiki). The game's massive success eventually birthed Super Mario Land 2: 6 Golden Coins and Wario Land, which launched Wario's own standalone spin-off series. While official re-releases have brought the classic to the Nintendo 3DS Virtual Console and Nintendo Switch Online, it's still nice to play this game again, albeit on the ZX Spectrum.

entry.title: The Legend of Zelda - Nintendo's hit game comes to the Commodore 64 via Goldfinger
entry.content:
The iconic NES classic The Legend of Zelda is making its way to the Commodore 64, thanks to a dedicated new port by developer Goldfinger. Built using Aldo Núñez’s commented Assembly source code from GitHub, this project aims to cram Nintendo's massive adventure onto an Easy Flash 3 cartridge. While Goldfinger’s current build slightly exceeds the original NES version's 128 KB limit, they plan to optimize and claw back precious memory during development. The game features full NTSC and PAL auto-detection, and features a complete overworld, dungeon levels, scrolling rooms, functional item screens, and progress saving directly to the cartridge.

Though the developer playfully describes the retro graphics as "lame," the port does have music, sound effects, an authentic attract-mode intro, and complete save-file character creation. Looking ahead, Goldfinger hopes to eventually implement native 1541 floppy disk support to mirror the game's original release on Nintendo's Famicom Disk System. While there are still a few minor bugs to iron out during upcoming playtests, the creator has noted that while game speeds are basically on par with the NES. And there's more to come, it's possible the C64 version could even play with no slowdowns (unlike the NES). Finally the developer's biggest hurdle may be legal; though Goldfinger wants to release the complete source code so the community can improve or repurpose the engine, copyright concerns regarding Nintendo's intellectual property leave the official public release up in the air.

entry.title: Lost Souls - Arcade horror from Megastyle for the C64 ( preorder boxed via Bitmap Soft)
entry.content:
Fancy playing another creepy game for Halloween weekend, then Megastyle has you covered with their latest game Lost Souls, an atmospheric arcade horror game that tasks players with saving a spirit trapped between worlds. Set within a forgotten, whisper-filled graveyard, the game requires players to brave a haunted path to ignite 25 lanterns resting upon ancient gravestones. However, players must work quickly against a strict time limit; all the lanterns must be lit before the clock strikes midnight, or the lost soul will remain trapped in the darkness forever.


The gameplay features tense moments with precise evasion as players navigate the cemetery's lower grounds to gather essential torches. While the creatures and shadows lurking in the dark won't outright end the player's life, a single touch from them will instantly banish the player back to the very beginning of their quest, wiping out precious progress. It is a high-stakes race against time where only perfect navigation and a steady hand will lift the veil, awaken the spirit, and restore the soul to peace.

entry.title: Big Ball Back Breaker - Bouncing balls in this new Commodore 64 game by Richard Bayliss of TND

entry.title: Ghouls 'n Ghosts - Modern Vintage Gamer sets out to improve an Amiga port of an Arcade classic
entry.content:
The 1989 Commodore Amiga port of Capcom’s arcade classic Ghouls 'n Ghosts looks to be getting a face-lift courtesy of Modern Vintage Gamer. While the original Software Creations port—published by U.S. Gold—was a respectable attempt for its time, it famously suffered from a common issue among era-specific ports by failing to utilise any of the Amiga’s powerful custom hardware. The new  enhancement directly addresses these shortcomings by injecting vibrant copper skies, an optimised, faster renderer, and a much-needed splash of colour into this classic game. Visually, the upgrade completely transforms the experience to introduce silky-smooth 50 Hz scrolling, fluid object motion, and a hardware-sprite-based Arthur.


Beyond the  graphical overhaul, the project’s development process also uncovered long-hidden secrets buried deep within the game's original code. However, Amiga purists will be glad to know that the core game logic remains entirely untouched, running at its exact native speed. Retro gamers should still expect some performance dips when the screen becomes cluttered with multiple large enemies, but the combination of hardware-driven fluidity and faithful gameplay makes this latest update a definitive love letter to Amiga enthusiasts.

entry.title: The Legend of the Little Chicken - Another fabulous ZX Spectrum game from Furillo Productions
entry.content:
Furillo Productions has unleashed They Called Him El Pollito (The Legend of the Little Chicken), a vibrant new shoot 'em up that injects a heavy dose of Spaghetti Western flair for the ZX Spectrum. Set in the lawless badlands of Bernard Valley, the game casts players as a feather-ruffling vigilante known simply as "The Chick." When the local schoolteacher and ultimate love interest, Rosita, is abruptly kidnapped, our gunslinging hero must hit the trail to rescue her. Rumours point to the notorious "Joe the Mad Miner" as the captor, but a deeper conspiracy suggests a much more powerful puppet master is pulling the strings from the shadows of this dusty frontier.


The game was built using a heavily customized version of Jonathan Cauldwell’s celebrated SEUD (Shoot-Em-Up Designer), seamlessly paired with Furillo Productions' own proprietary "ambush module" designed for the Mojon Twins’ MK1 engine. While the team behind this game has utilized some free asset libraries to flesh out environmental tiles like rocks and serpents, the core gameplay is a unique, high-energy arcade romp. For Spectrum fans looking for a fresh challenge, the stage is set, the revolver is loaded, and the fate of Bernard Valley rests entirely in your hands. As the website says "Now it's all up to you, Chick! Go get them!"

entry.title: The House on the Borderland - First person survival horror game for the C64 by AI/Michael Cox
entry.content:
Another C64 game to play with the release of The House on the Borderland, a first person survival horror game created by developer Michael Cox. Drawing direct inspiration from William Hope Hodgson’s classic 1908 novel, the game tasks players with a desperate stand to protect their home, their sister, and their loyal dog from an onslaught of marauding swine-things. Survival hinges on enduring three brutal nights of siege, where daylight hours must be carefully spent resting, repairing fortifications, and tending to the wounded. Compounding the tension is a strict lack of re-supply, forcing players to meticulously ration their starting stock across the entire ordeal while managing a unique "dread" meter. If this gauge climbs too high due to darkness, eerie silence, or structural damage, your character's perception will warp, leaving you completely paralysed by fear.

Although this game was created with assistance from Claude Code, the game according to the developer was extensively play-tested on actual Commodore 64 hardware. While the gameplay concept, intricate design, and retro graphics are entirely original creations, the game's audio design evolved uniquely during production; the music was carefully adapted over time, and the eerie sound effects actually originated as AI-generated placeholders that proved effective enough to be kept for the final release. So if this sounds like your sort of horror, make sure to check it out below.

entry.title: Tiltrune - A room flipping puzzler for the Amiga and C64 by AI/Gaboo Arts Entertainment
entry.content:
Gaboo Arts Entertainment with the help of AI has released Tiltrune, a clever new gravity-shifting puzzle game simultaneously targeting both the Amiga and the Commodore 64. The core mechanic turns the entire room into a mechanism, allowing players to rotate the screen left or right by 90 degrees. This rotation alters gravity, causing the explorer, crates, and gems to tumble into completely new configurations, effectively transforming what was once a blocking wall into a walkable floor. To succeed, players must meticulously plan their moves, pushing crates into position to absorb dangerous falls, dodging lethal spikes, and collecting every single gem before charting a path to the green exit.


The game boasts over 80 main puzzle rooms spread across five distinct vaults, alongside a special final chamber and unlockable post-game bonus challenges. Given the danger of falling debris, the developer has cleverly included a generous 100-state undo buffer and unlimited retries to encourage loose experimentation and creative problem-solving. Completing the package is a suite of features, including par targets, star ratings, and comprehensive performance statistics, all tied together by an animated end-of-run tally and disk-saved high scores.

  • TILTRUNE for Amiga brings our original Commodore 64 puzzle game (TILTRUNE C64 version) to the Commodore Amiga, with reworked graphics, animated title and reward screens, and Amiga music and sound effects. It preserves the original rooms, rules and controls.

Titled as 'Kizuna', this stylized black-and-white release frames its story through the lens of a classic comic book, using expressive pixel art to transform each game screen into a comic panel. The story follows the ninja Hanzo on a high-stakes mission to escort a young girl named Hana through a treacherous world cloaked in shadow. Rather than relying solely on mindless combat, the game challenges players with varied gameplay scenarios and obstacles that require patience, and clever problem-solving to overcome.

entry.title: Skyshift - This Arcade inspired Amstrad Shooter by TITAN looks well worth playing!
entry.content:
A rather fabulous arcade-inspired shooter has been released for the Amstrad CPC by Titan. Titled as 'Skyshift', the project draws heavy inspiration from classic vertical shooters like 1943. To maximize programming efficiency and ensure crisp readability on the Amstrad CPC, Titan has said that they have opted for a specialized 128x256 pixel gameplay window running in the Amstrad's distinct Mode 0. The game introduces players to a World War I Allied flying ace who, while dogfighting over the front lines in the spring of 1918, is suddenly swallowed by a bizarre, luminous cloud. He emerges into a radically changed sky, facing hyper-advanced, propellerless enemy aircraft that far outclass his fragile biplane.


Believing he has simply broken the time barrier and landed in 1945, the isolated pilot fights on alone against an increasingly improbable armada of jet engines and alien technologies. However, as the familiar landscapes morph into an eerie, unrecognizable landscape, a chilling truth begins to dawn. The cosmic phenomenon didn't just catapult him forward in time; it ripped him into an alternate reality entirely. marooned on a dystopian, parallel Earth where humanity has completely surrendered the skies to an oppressive alien empire, this lone multi-universal survivor must outmanoeuvre a relentlessly evolving military force to unlock the secrets of this strange dimension before his time runs out.

entry.title: IL MARINAIO - This latest Amstrad CPC 128k game by Andrea "Mr. DVG" Pastore is inspired by 1982 Arcade classic Popeye
entry.content:
Thanks to a heads up by Xenomorph we've been told that Andrea "Mr. DVG" Pastore has released their latest game of IL MARINAIO, a brand-new Amstrad CPC release built entirely from scratch in pure Z80 assembly language with the help of AI. Inspired by the iconic 1982 game Popeye from the arcades , the game hopefully captures the charm of the original. Players step into the shoes of a lovesick sailor tasked with catching hearts, musical notes, and love letters dropped from above by his sweetheart, all while staying clear of the freezing waters below. Standing in his way is a brutish bully who stalks the stages, alongside a bottle-flinging witch who begins hurling bouncing skulls at higher difficulty rounds. Fortunately, the classic spinach power-up makes a welcome return, granting temporary invincibility and allowing the nimble sailor to knock his rival into the sea with a satisfying punch.

The game unfolds across three faithfully recreated stages, packed with environmental mechanics with 16-colour Mode 0 graphics. Players will navigate the Docks to capture 24 hearts, utilizing a well-placed bucket to trap the bully's head; move to the Streets to gather 16 musical notes under a moon using a seesaw catapult; and finally board the Ship to spell out H-E-L-P, evading a diving bird to scale the main mast. As for game features, it runs at 25 updates per second using flicker-free double buffering, has custom AY-chip sound effects—including retro-styled crunch when landing a hit, and includes menus, high-score tracking, and gameplay configuration toggles to customize lives and starting levels.

Credits: programming by Claude (Anthropic) AI, direction by Mr. DVG.

entry.title: GODGAME - An in-dev Populous inspiration for the Amstrad CPC 6128!
entry.content:
A promising new god game is currently in development for the classic Amstrad CPC 6128 or a CPC with 128k of ram, drawing heavy inspiration from the legendary strategy title Populous. Titled as 'GODGAME', this in-development project by SoftDevil casts players in the role of a benevolent deity, easily identified by the bearded, crowned king avatar positioned in the top-left corner of the screen. The gameplay revolves around divine management and expansion, tasking you with guiding your loyal people as they settle flat lands and build up thriving residential villages.


Strategy is dictated entirely by numbers, where your overall divine strength is directly tied to the total population of your houses combined with the collective power of your citizens. The ultimate goal is a battle of demographic endurance against a rival deity; the moment you run out of followers, a "DEFEAT" screen marks your downfall while your opponent claims "VICTORY." Because the title is still right in the middle of development, the creator is actively seeking constructive feedback and feature suggestions from the Amstrad community to help shape the final release.

To survive the timer across each floor, players can grab piping-hot apple pies left on window sills by grateful residents, granting Felix temporary invincibility, brick-smashing power, and scoring multipliers.

entry.title: Enhanced framerate versions of Amiga games via AI and Vesuri
entry.content:
Vesuri with the help of AI is aiming to give many classic Amiga games a bit of a performance boost and some much needed bug fixes. For some time now, Amiga owners have faced a frustrating bottleneck: purchasing powerful hardware expansions—like the legendary Apollo 1240 accelerator card for the Amiga 1200—only to find that most classic games still struggled to run smoothly. Because early 90s software was rarely written for these faster, upgraded hardware setups, even the most expensive configurations left players disappointed. Drawing on extensive expertise from the Amiga demo scene, Vesuri recognized that the hardware was capable of far more, sparking a long-held ambition to patch these foundational software limitations to make the most out of powerful accelerators.

▶ Ver vídeo en YouTube

The breakthrough arrived after Vesuri successfully optimized the classic Stunt Car Racer to run at a blistering 50 frames per second. While that initial project required painstaking manual programming, recent technological leaps in artificial intelligence opened the door to a much faster, more scalable approach. By combining advanced AI tools with an intimate knowledge of the Amiga’s custom architecture, Vesuri is now actively releasing enhanced frame-rate versions of highly requested games on GitHub. These upgrades build directly upon existing WHDLoad infrastructure established by scene veterans like JOTD, Psygore, StingRay, and CFou!. To keep the installation process simple and avoid disrupting upstream maintainers, players can easily upgrade their experience by swapping out the original slave files, bringing enhanced performance updates to old classics. To see what's current being worked on with the latest video's it's worth visiting the website link all the way at the bottom.

  • Correct game speed and race timing regardless of rendering speed.
  • Experimental A4000 simulation for smoother, more responsive driving on faster PAL Amigas, selected by default on 68040/68060 systems.
  • Automatic simulation defaults and saved simulation preferences.
  • Replay saving and playback for A4000 mode; original replays remain supported.
  • A4000 jumps are closer to A2500; older A4000 replays are incompatible.

And that's just a small list of games that is currently getting much needed performance improvements and or big fixes for the Amiga. But for further developments and downloadable files hit the link (HERE)

entry.title: The Curse of Sherwood - Sunteam remakes a classic Mastertronic title for the PC!
entry.content:
Sunteam is back with some 8-bit nostalgia with their latest PC remake, The Curse of Sherwood. This latest release modernises a classic budget arcade adventure originally crafted by Derek Brewster and published by Mastertronic back in 1987 for the ZX Spectrum, Commodore 64, and Amstrad CPC. Heavily inspired by the iconic Spectrum edition, the game plunges players into an endangered Sherwood Forest, which has fallen under the tyrannical control of the sinister Cult of Sagalia. After Robin Hood and his Merry Men suffer a devastating defeat at the hands of the cult, a desperate Friar Tuck seeks the aid of the Bishop of Derby to perform a grand exorcism. However, the plan takes a dark turn when the Bishop is found dead, leaving behind a bloody parchment inscribed with a cryptic rhyme that holds the ultimate secret to destroying the cult once and for all.


▶ Ver vídeo en YouTube

Stepping into the sandals of Friar Tuck, players must navigate a treacherous, flick-screen world viewed from an elevated side angle to locate the artifacts necessary to complete the holy mission. Strategy is key, as Tuck's inventory is strictly limited to carrying just three items at a time, forcing players to think carefully about where and when to deploy their findings across the dense forest layout. The woodland paths are teeming with hostile creatures that will fire projectiles at any opportunity, and a single touch from these enemies or their weapons will cost you one of your three precious lives. Fortunately, the holy man isn't entirely defenseless; you can retaliate by throwing swords and gradually upgrading your arsenal to more powerful weaponry as you explore deeper into this charmingly reimagined retro quest from Sunteam.

AI Assisted, Sounds

  • We sourced music from Pixabay but did not realise that the tune used AI until it was near release and by then it just fitted the game so well that we decided not to change it. In future we will be more vigilant and do our best to source only human made audio.
